title: Trace enrichment plugin API for tenant metadata and rate limiting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a safe, extensible plugin interface in the trace ingestion pipeline that can enrich spans with per-tenant metadata, apply tenant-aware rate limits and sampling markers, and perform lightweight redaction. This work is intended to replace several ad-hoc post-processing rules we currently run in exporters and to centralize tenant-specific logic closer to ingest so downstream exporters (Tempo/Jaeger, S3 archives) receive normalized spans.
background_and_motivation: Customers running Redwood Private and Dedicated increasingly need per-tenant trace annotations (product, environment, customer-id hash) and enforcement of tenant quotas at ingest time to avoid noisy tenants overwhelming backends. Current solutions either mutate spans downstream (in exporters) or rely on brittle config maps. A plugin API gives us: (1) safe tenant-specific transformations that can be updated without deploys, (2) consistent sampling/quotas earlier in the pipeline, and (3) a place to centralize redaction/GDPR rules.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin interface (WASM runtime) integrated into otel-ingest service and configurable per-tenant
A reference tenant-enrichment plugin that attaches standardized attributes: tenant.id_hash, tenant.plan, tenant.region
Per-tenant rate-limiter hook callable from plugin that returns allow/deny with reason; metrics emitted
End-to-end test showing Tempo and Jaeger exporters receive enriched spans with unchanged traceIDs
Performance target: median plugin execution added latency < 2ms at 95th percentile for 128B span payloads
Canary rollout gated by feature flag 'trace-enrich-v1' with automated rollback on error-rate/regression
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Sandbox execution using WASM chosen for safety and hot-reloadability vs. running arbitrary JS/Python which risks resource exhaustion
We do enrichment at ingest (vs. exporter) to allow consistent sampling and quota enforcement earlier; cost is a small additional SLO risk on ingest path
Plugins are allowed to be 'read-only' to span.traceID and timing fields; mutation limited to attributes and tags to preserve signal integrity for linking with logs/metrics
Rate-limiter in-process uses leaky-bucket with memory cap; for high-cardinality tenants we fallback to an external throttler (edge case documented)
Non-blocking failure mode: plugin errors result in span passthrough + metrics and a tenant-scoped throttling fallback; we do not drop spans by default unless explicit deny returned
implementation_tasks: Add WASM plugin runner into trace-ingest worker with plugin lifecycle manager
Define plugin API spec (enrich(span), should_sample(span), get_tenant_quota(tenant_id)) and publish on Confluence
Build reference plugin: tenant-metadata-enricher + simple rate-limiter using tenant config from config-service
Expose metrics: plugin.exec_ms, plugin.errors_total, plugin_deny_count{tenant}, plugin_latency_histogram
End-to-end tests: unit tests for API, integration tests with Tempo and Jaeger test instances
Update exporters to honour plugin-applied sampling markers (trace.sampling_priority) where present
Create feature flag and rollout automation (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with canary health checks (error-rate, p95 latency, plugin_error_rate)
testing_plan: Unit tests for plugin API + WASM harness. Integration test harness runs a small Tempo and Jaeger instance in CI, sends synthetic high-cardinality tenant traffic and asserts enrichment attributes and sampling markers are present. Load test to measure added latency and tail behavior (k6 + internal load generator). Canary monitors: plugin_error_rate < 0.1% and p95 ingest latency regression < 10% compared to baseline.
rollout_and_mitigation: Rollout behind 'trace-enrich-v1' feature flag. Start with 1% traffic for 24 hours, validate canary dashboards. If plugin_error_rate > 0.5% or overall ingest error_rate increases by > 25% from baseline, immediate rollback. Post-rollout follow-up: increase sampling of high-cardinality tenants and enable external throttler for edge cases.
notes_and_risks: WASM execution sandbox must be audited for CPU/memory escapes; add runtime quotas and an accounting meter
Per-tenant config lookup must be cached carefully to avoid thundering herd on config-service
Risk of subtle downstream incompatibilities if plugins incorrectly mutate sampling markers; exporters must be defensive
Need legal signoff for any built-in redaction logic that might affect audit trails
